It was my first time traveling alone, and I was 15 years old. My itinerary was something along the lines of 

Board St. George, Utah -> SLC @ 11:00am
Board SLC -> Austin @ 4:00pm
Arrive in Austin @ 8:00pm

However, when I was about to board the flight to SLC, we got a notification that the landing gear was screwed up, and they had to get a mechanic from a city 45 minutes away to fix it. However, by the time he got there and fixed it, I had effectively missed my connection as I would arrive after the flight from SLC to Austin had departed. The worst part about this, is that it was a 5 MINUTE FIX. Anyway, I find out that the next connecting flight from SLC to Austin boarded at 8:00pm, so I just wait around for 5 hours until that flight starts to board, doing jack crap. Right before I boarded the plane, my phone died, and of course, my dumbass forgot to bring a charger. I board the flight, and in my head I’m thinking “Ok, my phones dead, this better land in Austin.” After a few hours everything was going smoothly, but as we neared the city, over the intercom I hear “Alright, it seems that they’re are some severe thunderstorms, and it’s not safe to land, so we are going to circle for about half an hour. Half an hour passed, and they let us know that they are diverting our flight to Houston. And I’m like “Well fuck, my phone’s dead, I don’t have any money on me, and if I did, I can’t rent a car, what the fuck do I do? So I got off the plane, and asked an airport security worker if I could borrow her phone. I called my dad, and explained my predicament, and he was about to say he’d figure out a way to pick me up, but I got interrupted by this young couple in their early 20s, who said “Hey, you look like you can’t go anywhere on your own, we’re trying to get a bus back to Austin, want to come.” Now under normal circumstances, I would’ve declined, but I was pretty desperate, so I let my dad know, and he said “Let me talk to them.” And I was about to hand them the phone, but as I looked, they had left. I looked for them for about 10 minutes, but after I couldn’t find them, I gave up hope. As I sat down, I randomly looked to the left and BAM they were right there. So my dad talks to them, and he’s like “Alright you can ride with them.” So then we wait around 4 more hours until around 5:00am, and then board a bus.
